title: role prompts carry the project's design from the engine side
acceptance: Why: portable prompts carry launcher-supplied role, approved immutable spec, bounded design/context with explicit cap and visible trimming, complete pinned gate contract, conventions whole, project+task/base and isolated checkout SHA. Trusted frozen launcher owns commit/push/publication outside rounds; no checkpoint command for workers to execute. No target-relative engine-file assumptions.

Roles use prompt-provided design/scope/conventions; dispatched role overrides startup routing. Firstmate works from engine root and supplies --project to supported project operations. After T-053, routine no-project dispatch fairly fills all projects; explicit --project only for captain-requested project work. Until implemented, report unsupported paths rather than claim external dispatch. Allocate all decision IDs through fm-decide.sh --allocate as D-<project>-<task>-<n>; no handpicked ranges.

Portable English roles refer to prompt-provided design, scope, conventions and launcher publication contract. No worker checkpoint execution and no obsolete D-999 decision range. Preserve self prompt shape and role separation.
The self project's prompt has the same shape; the reviewer still receives the diff, the spec and the design and never the worker's reasoning (R2).
Self-hosting keeps working after this task alone: with no --project, and with the firstmate-workflow project named explicitly, every existing caller, fixture and test behaves as before.
Evidence is this pull request's required GitHub check and the six gates 1,2,4,5,6,7. New behaviour gets tests written to fail first; the worker does not run the suite itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.

External project data lives only under FM_HOME/projects/<name>/{repo,worktrees,CONVENTIONS.md,tasks,design.md,state}. No private specs, worktrees, prompts, pins, evidence, mirrors or recovery data in engine state or its public tree. Private repos are accepted. Unreadable protection is unknown: require captain-confirmed project checks and policy before readiness, never infer permission or reject solely for visibility. Every GitHub operation names the project repository. Preserve self-project default and explicit-name compatibility. Never push to protected base; task-branch force-with-lease requires confirmed project policy and expected old head. Merge method, deletion, land/review/post and stacking follow CONVENTIONS.md, never hardcoded squash/delete.

Evidence: required GitHub checks and commit statuses plus six gates 1,2,4,5,6,7 on the authoritative current PR head; gate 3 is retired. Workers author feature-owned fail-first tests but run no suites. Tests stay at most 1200 lines; shared fixtures in tests/lib/ or tests/e2e/lib/, with literal helper references. Firstmate verifies CI/gates and real acceptance; a structure check cannot prove model compliance. Commit this task spec with implementation.

Before current-head acceptance, synchronize and verify the authoritative GitHub PR head against the local task ref and isolated checkout. Bind required check-runs AND commit statuses, gates, reviewed head/base/patch, reviewer identity/final-answer provenance and merge candidate to that verified SHA. If remote moves or cannot be verified, readiness is stale/unknown; refresh before accepting. Regression: GitHub update-branch moves remote while local ref remains stale; green local gates must not pass remote readiness. Approval carries only when authoritative current patch-id is unchanged and no later rejection supersedes it. Merge candidate binding is enforced at merge time by T-138 (`bin/fm-merge.sh`).

Regression must show prompt and isolated checkout refreshed after remote update-branch while local ref was stale, or explicit refusal before review. Reviewer receives machine evidence and authentic standing list, never worker reasoning. T-163 extraction alone does not establish remote-head freshness.
